provenance: AMD/Xilinx official Device Reliability Report UG116, SEU and Soft Error Rate Measurements. Vendor-published, beam-tested at LANSCE per JESD89A/89-3A. This is a NEUTRON / FIT cross-check anchor, NOT a heavy-ion sigma(LET) Weibull. Use only as a magnitude cross-check against the heavy-ion file weibull_7series_measured.json (handover doc section '源2'); do not mix particle species.

source.title: Device Reliability Report (UG116) - SEU and Soft Error Rate Measurements
source.measurement: LANSCE neutron beam testing per JESD89A/89-3A; real-time FIT per JESD89A/89-1A corrected for New York City
source.device_rows_used: 28 nm 'Kintex 7 and Virtex 7' (xc7vx690t belongs to this row)

unit_note: LANSCE Neutron Cross-Section per Bit is in cm^2/bit. FIT = failures per 1e9 device-hours; Mb = 1e6 memory bits. 90% confidence interval. These are single-energy neutron cross-sections and FIT rates; UG116 does NOT publish heavy-ion Weibull shape parameters (Lth/W/s).

CRAM.source: UG116 v10.20 Table 1, row '28 nm / Kintex 7 and Virtex 7'

BRAM.source: UG116 v10.20 Table 2, row '28 nm / Kintex 7 and Virtex 7'

FF.source: UG116 does not publish a user flip-flop (FF) cross-section; it covers CRAM, BRAM, URAM only.
FF.gap_note: No official FF value in UG116. Keep the heavy-ion FF value from Lee et al. 2014 (weibull_7series_measured.json) and flag as缺口 per handover.

crosscheck_note: Magnitude cross-check only. The heavy-ion sigma_sat in weibull_7series_measured.json (3.34e-12 .. 1.47e-11 cm^2/bit) is ~3 orders of magnitude above these neutron cross-sections (~5.6e-15 cm^2/bit). That is expected: heavy-ion sigma_sat is the saturated cross-section for high-LET ions, whereas UG116 is a single-energy atmospheric-neutron cross-section. Per handover A4, convert fitted heavy-ion sigma_sat to a neutron-equivalent FIT and compare against UG116; a >10x discrepancy requires written discussion.

independent_measured_neutron_sigma.source: Wirthlin, Takai, Harding, 2014 JINST 9 C01025, Table 1 (open access), Kintex-7 XC7K325T, LANSCE wide-spectrum neutron
independent_measured_neutron_sigma.vs_ug116_v10_20: CRAM 6.89e-15 vs 5.69e-15 (+21%), BRAM 6.15e-15 vs 5.57e-15 (+10%). Same order, same beam type, measured ~11 years apart: anchor CONFIRMED, well inside the 10x review threshold.

order_of_magnitude_fit_check.method: sigma x reference flux: 5.69e-15 cm2/bit x ~14 cm-2 h-1 (JEDEC JESD89A New York City sea-level reference condition, integral flux above ~10 MeV)
order_of_magnitude_fit_check.verdict: Same order of magnitude. Expected residual: the LANSCE single-energy sigma is not the full atmospheric spectrum response, and the UG116 real-time FIT is per JESD89A-89-1A with alpha and thermal-neutron contributions measured separately. Order-of-magnitude check PASSED (threshold 10x).

crosscheck_performed_2026_08_22.ug116_revision_check: 2026-08-22 web check: v10.20 (2025-07-23) still the latest indexed revision on docs.amd.com; UG116 is updated twice a year, re-check before citing in a paper.

layout_ecc_usage_note: Validation anchor only. Do NOT feed these neutron numbers into the heavy-ion Weibull kernel. Strike GUI flip_model=weibull uses weibull_7series_measured.json (Lee 2014 HI).

gaps.weibull_shape_parameters: UG116 gives neutron FIT, not heavy-ion Lth/W/s; shape parameters come from Lee et al. 2014
gaps.DVF_note: UG116 reports raw memory-cell SEU rates; functional soft error rate is lower by the Device Vulnerability Factor (typical DVF 5%, worst case 10%)
